description: Budget cuts can postpone maintenance prevention and preparedness until future crises become more costly.
Repeated crisis response becomes normalized while prevention and adaptation remain underfunded.
Efficiency-focused policy may face opposition if public voice and equity are weak.
Powerful incumbent interests may shape industrial transition policy to preserve rents.
Participation can become symbolic if community input does not alter decisions or budgets.
Resilient equity-oriented policy can be weakened if funding and delivery capacity are inadequate.
Preparedness systems can decay between crises if political attention and funding fade.
Long-horizon adaptive policy can fail if monitoring triggers and budgets are not operationalized.
